items.title: An object of the derived category is invertible exactly when it is locally a shift of the ring, and then its cohomology is finite projective in a single degree per factor
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and an object M of D(R) and gives two equivalent conditions: that M be invertible with respect to the tensor product in D(R); and that for every prime p there exist f not in p and an integer n with M_f isomorphic to R_f[-n]. It then asserts four consequences in the invertible case: that M is perfect; that M is the direct sum of its shifted cohomology objects; that each H^n(M) is a finite projective module; and that R decomposes as a product over a range of degrees on which the corresponding cohomology module is invertible (source lines 38656-38675). The proof is a real local-to-global argument. For (2) implies (1) it forms R Hom_R(M, R) and the composition map R Hom(M, R) tensor^L_R M -> R, sees by local checking that this is an isomorphism in a step stated to be omitted, and concludes that M is invertible because D(R) is symmetric monoidal (proof lines 38678-38683). For (1) implies (2) it observes that an invertible object of a monoidal category has a left dual, namely its inverse, so M is perfect by the duals-and-perfection lemma; then for a prime p with residue field kappa it uses that M tensor^L_R kappa is an invertible object of D(kappa), which forces dim H^i(M tensor^L_R kappa) to be nonzero for exactly one i and equal to 1 there, and the lift-perfect-from-residue-field lemma then produces the required n (proof lines 38686-38695). The last part is the global assembly: the proof defines U_n as the union of the opens D(f) with M_f isomorphic to R_f[-n], notes U_n and U_{n'} are disjoint for n not equal to n', and if M has tor amplitude in [a, b] then U_n is empty for n outside that range; hence there is a product decomposition R = prod_{a <= n <= b} R_n with U_n corresponding to Spec(R_n), and since D(R) decomposes as the product of the D(R_n) the remaining assertions (b), (c) and (d) follow (proof lines 38698-38707). The non-routine content is the residue-field argument that forces the single-degree shape, and the product decomposition that promotes it to a global statement.
